The British footprints of Istanbul, on foot

A map and pocket guide to 51 places where British travellers, soldiers, diplomats, architects and artists left their mark on Istanbul – from the Crimean War barracks at Scutari to the embassies of Pera. Pick a place, read its story, and walk there.

What's inside

Every place sits on the map, grouped by theme. Tap it for the story, the pictures and a short note on visiting.

51 places with their stories

Embassies and consulates, Crimean War barracks and cemeteries, Anglican churches, British-built banks, schools and railways, writers' haunts and film locations – each with a story, its period, its district and visiting notes.

7 self-guided walks

From the Asian shore at Üsküdar through British Pera, along the Bosphorus by ferry, to Kadıköy and Moda and the old city in Victorian engravings. Each walk is a route of numbered stops.

Victorian engravings, then and now

See Istanbul as Bartlett, Allom and other Victorian artists drew it, then stand on the same spot today. Historic and modern pictures, all freely licensed and credited.

Pictures that work offline

The stories and all the pictures are inside the app, so they work without mobile data. Only the street map loads over the internet.

Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps

Tap Directions to walk to a place, or hand a whole walk to your maps app with one button.

Your location stays on your phone

Distances and the “you are here” dot are worked out on the phone. No account, no ads, no tracking.

Questions and answers

Is this a self-guided walking tour of Istanbul?

Yes. The seven walks are self-guided routes with numbered stops and a story at each one. You walk at your own pace, and the app hands the stops to Apple Maps or Google Maps for walking directions.

Which places are in the app?

51 places linked to British history in Istanbul, for example Selimiye Barracks and the Haidar Pasha British war cemetery at Scutari, Pera House and the summer embassy at Tarabya, the Crimean Memorial Church, the Ottoman Bank in Galata, the Tünel railway, the British village of Moda in Kadıköy and the viewpoints of the Victorian engravers.

Does it work offline?

The stories and all the pictures are inside the app and work without a connection. The street map comes from OpenStreetMap and needs mobile data or Wi-Fi.

What is free, and what does the unlock include?

The map, a first look at every place and the whole Üsküdar walk are free. One purchase unlocks all 51 stories, all 7 walks, every picture, directions to every place and future content updates.

Is it a subscription?

No. It is a one-time purchase with no ads. On another phone or after reinstalling, use “Restore purchases” with the same Apple ID or Google account.

Which languages does it speak?

English and Turkish. You can switch the language in the app's settings.

Do I need to be in Istanbul to use it?

No. You can read the stories and plan your walks at home. Distances and the “you are here” dot appear once you are in the city and allow location access.

Does the app track me?

No. There is no account, no advertising and no tracking. The app sends anonymous usage statistics that you can switch off in Settings; the privacy policy lists exactly what they contain.
